memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses said to them, 'No one is to keep any of it until morning.' However,
some of them paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, but
it was full of maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them."
- Ex 16:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Some of them hoarded, and it rotted.

We should understand why they did it. They were people who had been hungry
three days ago. Keeping some back felt like ordinary prudence, and to human eyes
it looked wise.

But God had said no, and there was a reason. Hoarded manna would have quietly
replaced trust. A jar in the corner means you do not need to look up tomorrow
morning. God was protecting their dependence, which is another way of saying He
was protecting their relationship with Him.

Notice that the manna did not rot because manna was fragile. It rotted on the
days it was hoarded and kept perfectly on the Sabbath, as we will see. The
spoiling was purposeful.

Jesus told a parable about a man who built bigger barns and said to his soul,
"Take life easy; eat, drink and be merry." God's verdict was: "You fool! This
very night your life will be demanded from you" (Luke 12:19-20). The problem was
not the harvest. It was where the man had placed his security.

There is a difference between wise saving, which Scripture commends, and hoarding
that quietly replaces trust in God. The heart knows which it is doing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you are holding on to that is quietly replacing trust?
2. What is the difference, in your life, between prudence and anxiety?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me where I am storing up out of fear rather than wisdom. Help me to
depend on You daily. Amen.
